PostgreSQL 19 is in release candidate testing, and the latest minor releases are 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, and 14.24.

- **PostgreSQL 19:** RC 1 came out on October 15, 2026. The release team plans to issue a second release candidate, PostgreSQL 19 RC 2, on November 12, 2026. Unless an issue is discovered that requires a delay or an additional release candidate, PostgreSQL 19 should be made generally available on November 19, 2026.
- **Latest minors:** The most recent batch of minor releases covers 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, and 14.24. This release skips PostgreSQL 18 versions from PostgreSQL 18.4 to 18.6. 18.5 was not shipped due to a regression. The next scheduled update release is also set for November 12, 2026, and will include a large number of fixes.
- **End-of-life:** PostgreSQL 14 will stop receiving fixes on November 12, 2026.
- **Versioning policy:** The PostgreSQL Global Development Group releases a new major version containing new features about once a year. Each major version receives bug fixes and, if need be, security fixes that are released at least once every three months in what we call a "minor release." The PostgreSQL Global Development Group supports a major version for 5 years after its initial release.

The search did not give an exact date for the 18.6 batch. Its listing is about two months old, so check the release notes page for the current latest patch numbers before relying on them.

content.text:
As of today (2026-10-17), the newest stable PostgreSQL is **18.6**. PostgreSQL 19 is not out yet.

- **Current stable:** 18.6 is the latest minor of the 18 series. The same batch also shipped 17.11, 16.15, 15.19 and 14.24.
- **PostgreSQL 19:** RC 1 came out on October 15, 2026. RC 2 is planned for November 12, and general availability is planned for November 19, barring problems. Don't use it for production yet.
- **Next minor release:** The next scheduled update is November 12, 2026.
- **End of life:** PostgreSQL 14 stops getting fixes on November 12, 2026. If your image is on 14, plan an upgrade.

The search results didn't give an exact date for the 18.6 release, and 18.5 was skipped because of a regression. Check the [release notes page](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/) to confirm 18.6 is still the latest patch.

For the Docker image, `postgres:18` follows the latest 18.x minor, and `postgres:18.6` pins that exact version. If you pin a tag, you can check it against the first command below. You can also run the second command inside a running container to see which version it has.

```
docker pull postgres:18 && docker run --rm postgres:18 postgres --version
docker exec <container> postgres --version
```

If you tell me where the Dockerfile or compose file is, I can check which tag you're on.
